good: The eastern outskirts (Warschau, Posen, Białystok) show what the user asked for: pastel single-family houses with hipped roofs, picket fences, birches, Plattenbau on the horizon. The Kulturpalast is visible from the City Limits on.

The Balkan outskirts (Belgrad, Sofia, Slavonski Brod) are very recognisable: unplastered brick houses with rebar on the roofs, garden walls, a red-and-white Serbian-Byzantine church (city_balkan_church).
Bern: Swiss chalets with spruces in the outskirts; arcaded Laubenhäuser with flower boxes in the centre.

Wien: Schönbrunn-yellow palais with green roofs and a Karlskirche-style church. Riesenrad (red wheel) and Stephansdom (zig-zag roof) are recognisable from far away and while passing. The Reichsbrücke has water on both sides. At night the Riesenrad lights and the Stephansdom illumination look good.

Prag, Budapest, Ljubljana centres: pastel baroque gables and Jugendstil houses read as Central European old towns. The Budapest Parliament (red roofs, dome, spires) is recognisable from the outskirts (A#09) through to the bridge.

Venedig: the Ponte della Libertà causeway, with lagoon water on both sides, concrete parapets and lamps every 36 m, plus the Campanile and San Marco on the horizon, is the classic arrival view. Night shows lit lamps and the lit Campanile.
Mailand: the Duomo (white Gothic with spires) is recognisable when passing; high-rises in the background skyline.
Sofia: the Alexander-Newski cathedral (white, green and gold domes) is recognisable from about 170 m.
Nürnberg: Fachwerk and baroque houses; the Kaiserburg on its rock plinth is recognisable from 2-4 km and lit warm at night.

Stone-arch bridges (München Maximiliansbrücke, Prag Most Legií, Ljubljana Drachenbrücke, Warschau Poniatowski): stone balustrades, three-globe candelabra, water on both sides, glowing lamps with reflections at night. Steel-railing river bridges (Wien, Posen, Slavonski Brod, Nürnberg): no gaps or z-fighting seen.

Landmarks show no pop-in. They fade in from the City Limits (prop range 1900 m) and appear at plausible size and distance, with no double silhouettes. At night windows are lit and landmarks illuminated (Riesenrad, Stephansdom, Campanile, Kaiserburg, Kulturpalast).
No fallback buildings appear in these 7 styles: every props/city_* set referenced by german_old, vienna, central, swiss, italian, balkan and eastern exists, and nothing falls back to tinted generics.
No errors in the 45 runs, only ObjectDB leak warnings at exit. City Limits entry (banner, 50 sign, crosswalk, 40 m clear zone, 2.5 s background blend) works.

Performance: headless bench_render.gd at city positions (Wien, Belgrad, Venedig, Warschau, Prag; load about 3.5 on 4 cores) gave medians of 5.1-9.0 ms versus 5.1-10.1 ms at km 100 of the same stages. Draw commands rise from 21-43 to 33-65 in the outskirts. No slowdowns seen.

good: Amsterdam reads unmistakably as Amsterdam: canal houses with step and bell gables on both sides, 5 grachten with wrought-iron railings, brick quay walls, green houseboats sitting at the waterline, bridge names in the HUD, the blue Dutch City Limits sign, and brick terraces with hedges and poplars in the outskirts. At night, lit windows over dark water (contact/amsterdam.png).

Hamburg's arrival is strong: the Köhlbrandbrücke approach, then the Elbbrücken with green truss portals every 40 m, side girders, water on both sides and a ship. The Elbphilharmonie and Michel stand across the Elbe (shots/hamburg/out_bridge_00.png, km 83.8), followed by the Speicherstadt. At night the portals and the lit Elbphilharmonie work well.
Berlin: the Fernsehturm is seen whole with its sphere from the City Limits onward (out_day_01..04). The Gründerzeit centre fits, and the Oberbaumbrücke has a red balustrade with lamps over water.
Dresden: the Frauenkirche sprite is recognisable from the Augustusbrücke, the Canaletto view, and floodlit at night. The sandstone balustrade and three-globe lamps are right.
Frankfurt: the Mainhattan skyline sprite (Messeturm pyramid, bank towers) is visible from the City Limits and lit at night. The Friedensbrücke railing and water are fine.
Würzburg and Erfurt: the german_old mix of half-timbered and baroque houses with picket fences suits Franconia and Thuringia. The Ludwigsbrücke balustrade and lit lamps with reflections are good.
Kiel Holtenauer Hochbrücke: high deck (16 m), green embankments, a ship in the canal below. The far embankment filling the mid-distance is physically plausible.
Landmarks just after a bridge make good compositions across the water: Bremer Dom (Weser), Magdeburger Dom (Elbe), Martinskirche (Fulda), and Hannover (Leine).

Bridges in all cities: water level, quay walls and banks, all railing types (steel, balustrade, iron) and lamps are correct. No gaps, z-fighting or floating decks at either end of any of the 11 bridges checked. No scenery stands on the water.

City Limits entry: the motorway narrows to a two-lane city road with City Limits signs on both sides, a 50 sign and a zebra crossing. The transition from outskirts to centre is smooth, with the backdrop blending (contact/transitions.png).

Scale is sensible: office towers in the german centre are capped at 47–65 m (city_german_office scale 0.36–0.5), so no 100 m towers in Kassel or Magdeburg. The Leipzig City-Hochhaus has the right height. Buildings neither float nor stand on the road or sidewalk; hedges and picket fences with driveway gaps look fine.
No pop-in: the Fernsehturm, Florianturm and Frankfurt skyline fade in through the haze at the City Limits (landmark_fade).

Performance is fine (perf/bench.txt, headless _draw under load from parallel runs). Medians: 5.0–7.6 ms by day and 5.6–9.3 ms at night in city and bridge positions, against 5.2–6.9 ms outside the city. Minimums on the bridges are 5.4–6.8 ms, in line with docs/staedte.md §7. result.summary:
I fixed all high and medium findings and most of the low ones, mainly through data changes in data/cities.json and data/scenery.json. Code changes are in track.gd, road_renderer.gd, backdrop.gd and city_data.gd. Everything is committed in the worktree (not pushed).

Main code fixes:
- Cable-stayed bridge pylons now always use the procedural pylon, via a new prop flag `prefer_proc`.
- Landmark park trees are never placed on or within 8 m of a bridge (`Track.near_bridge`).
- Skyline entries that have a procedural form draw it instead of the generic fallback sprite.
- Churches used as landmarks (`props/church`) are floodlit at night.
- The mountain range behind a city takes `color` and `haze` from the data.
- The ground blends from outskirts to centre over the last 150 m.
- Close up, the Cuatro Torres get floor bands and the domed buildings get rows of windows.
- Domed buildings can drop the cross on top.
- New procedural form `octagon` for the Herkules in Kassel.

New styles: `german_east` (Magdeburg, Leipzig), `ruhr` (Dortmund), `bavarian` (München), `french_south` (Lyon, Bordeaux, Toulouse, Montpellier) and `spanish_north` (San Sebastián, Burgos). Dresden now uses `central`. Many landmarks were moved or replaced, including the Eiffel tower and Pont Alexandre III. Left-side trees in all city sceneries are mirrored. Hamburg's centre has gabled houses instead of the Speicher wall, and Wien has Zinshäuser.

New regression tests:
- Park trees stay off bridges, on a test track and in every real arrival. Both tests fail without the fix.
- Pylons are drawn procedurally.
- Skyline entries use their procedural form.
- Mountain range colour and haze.
- Ground blend.
- Every style, including the new ones, is checked and its trees are mirrored.

Test results:
- `tools/run_tests.sh`: 336 unit tests, 0 failed.
- Integration checks: all OK.
- Police-escape check: OK.
- Exit code 0.

About 80 screenshot runs (1280×720) were rendered at the same positions as the QA runs. Where no QA shot existed for a position, the "before" image came from an unmodified copy of the project. 27 before/after contact sheets are in the scratchpad folder `cities/qa/fix/`.
